All areas served

Renovation on the French side of Geneva.

From its base in Gex, Création & Rénovation Gessienne works on masonry and interior improvement projects in the French Genevois. The first conversation covers the work itself, as well as access to the property and how it will be used while the work takes place.

Describe my project in this area

For an apartment, clarify access.

The floor level, lift, width of passageways and parking options influence planning. If shared areas need to be crossed, explain the access conditions and any instructions you have received. These details help prepare the movement of materials and protective measures before the working arrangements are agreed.

In a house, consider how rooms connect.

A new partition, a wall repair or a change of flooring can affect circulation and the junctions between rooms. Describe the result you want and the elements to retain. Assessing the existing surfaces then helps identify the masonry, plastering or tiling work that genuinely fits the project.

Describe the property, not just the town.

Whether in Annemasse, Gaillard and Étrembières, or around Collonges-sous-Salève, Bossey and Saint-Julien-en-Genevois, every address has its own constraints. Include the property type, rooms involved, whether they will remain occupied and your preferred timeframe. This information supports the assessment; it is not a booking or a quotation.

Explore the services to identify the work on your walls, layout and finishes.

Before you begin.

How should I prepare for work in a shared building?

Tell us the floor level, delivery options, shared areas to cross and any instructions from the building management. Mention known access or timing restrictions so they can be considered when planning the work.

How should I prepare work in an occupied home?

Explain which rooms need to remain usable, which routes need to stay open and any everyday constraints. This helps us discuss a suitable scope and plan before any commitment is made.
